captions: Hello, and welcome to Camday English, Stage 7. In this lesson: Why do volcanoes erupt?
Read an explanation and use cause-and-effect connectives.
Here are some new words. Magma. Hot liquid rock under the Earth's surface. Pressure.
The force of something pushing on something else. Crust. The hard outer layer of the Earth.
And some more words. Tectonic plate. A huge piece of the Earth's crust that moves slowly. Consequently.
As a result. Gradually. Slowly, over a period of time.
Time for a question. The video will stop. Which word means: hot liquid rock under the Earth's surface?
Now some grammar: Cause and effect.
Use because, as a result, consequently, therefore and this causes to explain why things happen.
For example: The plates move. As a result, earthquakes happen.
For example: Pressure builds up because gas is trapped.
Now listen, and read along. Why do volcanoes erupt?
Deep under the Earth's crust, the temperature is so high that some rock melts into a liquid called magma.
Magma is lighter than the solid rock around it, so it rises slowly towards the surface.
It often collects in a magma chamber a few kilometres underground.
Magma contains gases such as water vapour and carbon dioxide.
As more magma gathers, these gases are trapped and the pressure gradually increases.
When the pressure becomes greater than the strength of the rock above, the rock cracks.
Consequently, magma, gas and ash burst out through the opening. This is an eruption.
Once magma reaches the surface, it is called lava.
Many volcanoes form where tectonic plates meet, because the crust there is thinner and weaker.
Another question. The video will stop. What is magma?
Well done! Today you learned new words, like magma, pressure, crust. You practised cause and effect.
And you read Why do volcanoes erupt? Now try the practice questions. See you next time!

captions: Hello, and welcome to Camday English, Stage 7. In this lesson: It happens every time.
Use the zero conditional for scientific facts and the passive with modal verbs.
Here are some new words. Evaporate. Change from liquid to gas. Condense. Change from gas to liquid. Freeze.
Become solid because it is very cold.
And some more words. Cycle. A set of events that happens again and again. Absorb. Take in a liquid or gas.
Reflect. Send back light, heat or sound.
Time for a question. The video will stop. Which word means: change from liquid to gas?
Now some grammar: Zero conditional and modal passives.
Use If, When plus present simple, present simple for things that are always true.
Use can, must, should plus be plus past participle for modal passives.
For example: If you heat ice, it melts. For example: Water can be turned into steam.
For example: Plastic should be recycled.
Now listen, and read along. The water cycle. The water on Earth is always moving in a cycle.
When the sun heats the sea, lakes and rivers, some of the water evaporates and becomes water vapour,
an invisible gas. The warm, moist air rises. If air rises high into the sky, it cools.
When water vapour cools, it condenses into tiny droplets, which form clouds.
When the droplets join together and become too heavy, they fall as rain, or as snow if the air is very cold.
The water flows into rivers and back to the sea, or it is absorbed into the ground,
where it can be used by plants. Then the cycle begins again.
Another question. The video will stop. What does the sun do to the water in the sea?
Well done! Today you learned new words, like evaporate, condense, freeze.
You practised zero conditional and modal passives. And you read The water cycle.
Now try the practice questions. See you next time!
